A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEnvAgent work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The original Appendix G is retained as Appendix I in v3, allowing its content to be distinguished from the new Appendices G and H.

before.justification: v1 reports original MEnvBench evaluations, reuse ablations, failure analyses, dataset construction statistics, and downstream fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds a multilingual reuse ablation and quantified C++ failure analysis.

M1.justification: The Planning-Execution-Verification architecture, environment retrieval, incremental patching, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Appendix H's proposed resource-adaptive sandboxes and specialized tools are future work.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same MEnvBench languages and tasks, MEnvData-SWE coverage, and downstream evaluation benchmarks. The new analyses examine subsets and failures within existing MEnvBench coverage.

E2.justification: The Repo2Run, SWE-Bench-Live, and SWE-Factory comparisons retain their language applicability, and Table 4's model comparisons are unchanged. The new ablation uses the existing w/o Reuse variant; the original w/o EnvPatchAgent comparison remains.

E3.justification: v3 Appendix G introduces a 200-task ablation design: ten languages, four repositories per language, and five instances per repository. This supplements the retained Python ablation with up to ten instances per repository; existing benchmark and training protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially broadens component validation beyond v1's Python reuse ablation through a comparison across all ten languages. Appendix H also adds five quantified C++ failure categories and repository examples, extending the earlier broad outcome breakdown into a detailed diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added averages and failure percentages continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 11 reports average PASS of 46.5% versus 38.0% without reuse, RSR of 21.5%, and TIME of 4,069 versus 5,025 seconds. Appendix H adds failure frequencies, including 22% for compilation memory exhaustion and 20% for build-system incompatibility. These supplementary results leave the original Tables 2-4 and 9-10 unchanged.

T1.justification: The state-transition, verification, and environment-adaptation formulations in Sections 2-3 and Appendix B, including Equations 1-8, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same framework, benchmark, and dataset contributions, including the headline 8.6-percentage-point F2P gain and 43% time reduction. The added analyses support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix H expands the earlier compilation/resource explanation into specific memory, build-system, dependency, and network limitations, interpreting the bottlenecks as largely structural and infrastructural. Appendix G additionally interprets the observed per-language gains as evidence of universal reuse efficacy.

D1.justification: Agent specifications, Algorithm 1, Table 8's hyperparameters, the resource-access link, and training hardware and optimization details are unchanged. The training implementation material moves from Appendix G.6 to I.6 without substantive revision.

R1.justification: Section 7, Appendix A, the bibliography, and the comparison with existing datasets retain the same cited works and research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized front-matter, heading, and cross-reference edits, adds Appendix sections G and H, and renames the former G as I. Most existing prose remains verbatim, with no extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 11, reflows the final appendices, and renumbers the existing dataset tables as Tables 12-13. All ten original figures and existing table designs are retained; running headers are corrected to the paper title.

improvement.justification: The multilingual ablation supplies direct support beyond v1's Python-only component study, while the C++ diagnosis makes practical limitations more concrete. These additions modestly strengthen the paper. Their value is limited by Table 11's conflicting descriptions of RSR and Appendix H's unspecified denominators for failure percentages; the core experiments remain unchanged.
